raw_response:
I've been working this land for 35 years. I know Quzhou's soil and seasons better than I know anything else. My farm is 7 mu — not big, just me and my wife. I have to be careful with money and labor, but I also know what sells at the county market.

**My thinking:**

The chili-cabbage rotation is the heart of my operation. I put 4 mu into it. Chili goes in the ground in late March after the last frost — I'll start the seedlings in February indoors. I always use hybrid seed now. I switched maybe 15 years ago when my neighbor's hybrid chili yielded nearly double mine. I won't go back to traditional. After chili harvest in August, I rotary-till that same 4 mu and transplant autumn cabbage. Cabbage is my cash crop — the market at Quzhou always wants cabbage in November.

My remaining 2 mu I put into summer maize. It's not glamorous but it's reliable. I plant郑单958 or similar hybrid, same as everyone around here. It feeds the household and I sell what's left.

The last 1 mu I use for spinach in autumn. It fills the gap after I clear some plots, and my wife handles most of it. We eat some and sell the rest fresh at the village market. Spinach doesn't need much — a few irrigations from the well, some urea, and it's done.

Water: my well irrigation is reliable. I irrigate chili frequently in July heat. Cabbage needs water at transplant and during head formation. Maize I watch closely at silking — that's when water stress kills yield.

Pesticides: I'm careful. Chili gets hit by aphids and anthracnose every year, so I spray when I see them — I don't spray on a fixed calendar anymore, I learned that wastes money. Cabbage gets cabbage looper and aphids. Maize usually just needs corn borer treatment once or twice.
